## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: One failed SendGrid cancel blocks all later cancellations, forever

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-77

Explanation:
The whole loop sits inside a single `try`. If any `client.request` throws, the loop stops. The remaining reminders are never cancelled, and the deletes queued so far are never awaited.

The query uses `lte: now + 1h` with no lower bound, so it also matches reminders whose send time has already passed. Cancelling an already-sent or invalid `batch_id` can fail at SendGrid. That failing row is never deleted, so it is picked up again on every cron run and fails again.

Rows are returned in the same order each run, so every reminder after the bad one is never cancelled. Those emails go out for bookings that were cancelled or rescheduled.

The requests are also awaited one at a time, which makes the cron slower as the backlog grows.

Fix: wrap each reminder in its own `try/catch`. Always delete the DB row, or at least delete rows whose `scheduledDate` has passed. Consider running the requests in parallel.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
await Promise.allSettled(
  remindersToCancel.map(async (reminder) => {
    try {
      if (reminder.referenceId && dayjs(reminder.scheduledDate).isAfter(dayjs())) {
        await client.request({
          url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends",
          method: "POST",
          body: { batch_id: reminder.referenceId, status: "cancel" },
        });
      }
    } catch (e) {
      console.log(`Error cancelling scheduled email ${reminder.id}: ${e}`);
    } finally {
      await prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminder.id } }).catch(() => null);
    }
  })
);
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: `immediateDelete` path cancels at SendGrid but never removes the DB row

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213-223
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964-975

Explanation:
When `immediateDelete` is true, the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns. It never deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row.

- For the workflow-delete and step-delete callers in `workflows.tsx`, the cascade from `WorkflowStep` may clean the row up. That relationship is outside this diff, so I have not verified it.
- In `handleNewBooking`, nothing removes the row. The original booking is left with a reminder that is still `scheduled: true` and has a `referenceId`, but the batch behind it no longer exists at SendGrid.

The previous code also called `DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/{id}`. That call is now gone, so cancelled batches pile up on the SendGrid account.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
if (immediateDelete) {
  await client.request({
    url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends",
    method: "POST",
    body: { batch_id: referenceId, status: "cancel" },
  });
  await prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } });
  return;
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Reliability
Title: Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget (unawaited promises)

Affected:
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:484-495
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:487-494
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964-975
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:212-218,376-382,519-525,574-580

Explanation:
The old code collected the DB deletes and awaited them with `Promise.all`. The new code calls the async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` inside `forEach` without awaiting them.

On serverless (Vercel/Next API routes) the function can be frozen once the response is sent. When that happens, the `cancelled` update, the row delete, or the Twilio/SendGrid cancel may never run, and the reminders are still sent.

The `try/catch` in `handleNewBooking` cannot catch any of these rejections, so it does nothing.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
await Promise.all(
  originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.map((reminder) =>
    reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL
      ? deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)
      : reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.SMS
      ? deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)
      : Promise.resolve()
  )
);
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Security
Title: Ownership scope dropped from reminder deletion

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376-382

Explanation:
The old code deleted reminders with `where: { id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id } }`, which limited deletes to the caller's own bookings. The new helpers delete or update by `id` only.

This is only safe if `remindersToDeletePromise` already restricts results to the current user's bookings. That query is outside the diff, so I could not confirm it, hence the reduced severity.

Fix: confirm the upstream query filters by `booking.userId`. Alternatively, keep the ownership filter, for example by having the helpers use `deleteMany`/`updateMany` with that filter.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
// ensure upstream query includes:
where: { booking: { userId: ctx.user.id, eventTypeId: ... } }
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Type-only imports converted to value imports; possibly unused imports

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:1-10
- packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1-10

Explanation:
Several types are now imported as runtime values:
- `workflows.tsx`: `PrismaPromise` and `Prisma`. Their remaining uses were removed in this diff, so they may now be unused.
- `handleNewBooking.ts`: `App`, `Credential` and `EventTypeCustomInput`.

Under `isolatedModules` or `importsNotUsedAsValues`/`verbatimModuleSyntax` settings, these can cause lint or build errors. They also pull type-only symbols into the runtime import.

Fix: restore `import type` for the type-only symbols and remove any imports that are no longer used.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
import type { App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, Prisma } from "@prisma/client";
import { BookingStatus, SchedulingType, WebhookTriggerEvents, WorkflowMethods } from "@prisma/client";
~~~

Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
